text:
Ashwin: Quick status — ran a hybrid tracing experiment on staging GPUs to measure profiler overhead vs SLA impact. Approach: tiny continuous sampling (0.5% of requests) + short full nsys bursts (200ms) every 5m. Results below.

Lisa: Nice, can you paste the numbers (p50/p95/p99, overhead %) so we can decide guardrails?

Ashwin: Summary numbers from 2hr run: continuous 0.5% sampling => ~+0.8% mean token latency, p95 +0.9%, p99 +1.1%. Bursts (200ms every 5m) when they occurred added short spikes: measured local p99 increase of +2.1% during burst windows, but averaged over full run p99 delta ~+0.3%. GPU overhead (measured by nvml): sampling steady-state +1.2% GPU util, burst periods +8-11% util. Overall cost = ~2.3% extra GPU time if run continuously at this cadence.

Jordan: Which kernels dominated during the burst spikes?

Ashwin: Top hotspots during bursts (nsys timeline):
```
multi_head_attention_fwd            42.3ms total (burst window)
fused_gelu                         12.8ms
softmax_layer_norm                  9.5ms
kv_cache_read                         3.1ms  (not huge but lots of launches)
memset / cudaMemcpy                  6.7ms
```
Most of the extra time is attention fwd breakdown and kernel launch overheads (many tiny CUDA kernels from KV cache path).

Samir: Can you share the nsys command and nvtx markers you used so we can reproduce?

Ashwin: Repro snippet we used (simplified):
```
# start continuous low-sample collector (user-level sampling, lightweight)
python infra/trace_runner.py --mode=low-sample --rate=0.005 --out=s3://redwood-traces/hybrid/low

# trigger short full capture via NVTX for 200ms every 5m
# service emits NVTX push/pop around request handler; capture range set in nsys
nsys profile -o hybrid_burst --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-include=rt_marker --duration-limit=200ms --sample=none --target-processes=all --output=hybrid_burst.qdrep
```
Note: our runner toggles a "trace_burst" NVTX marker from the service so nsys captures only the 200ms window.

Lisa: Nice. From a production-safety standpoint we need a deterministic throttle policy. Propose: if any of these hold -> disable bursts for 10m and drop sampling rate by half:
- p99 latency regression > +1.5% over baseline
- perf.trace.overhead_pct > 3% averaged over 5m
- GPU util > 96% and sustained > 60s
That should keep customer-facing routes safe.

Jordan: Also suggest route-level opt-out for high-SLO routes (embedding endpoints, realtime chat). Some routes can stay at 0.05% sampling only; others can accept bursts.

Ashwin: Agreed. Implementation notes:
- Telemetry metrics to emit: perf.trace.overhead_pct, perf.trace.burst_count, perf.trace.last_burst_ts, perf.trace.throttle_state.
- Throttle state transitions: OK -> CAPPED (reduce burst length to 50ms) -> PAUSED (no bursts) -> COOLING (wait 10m) -> OK.
- Make burst duration and cadence configurable per deployment and route.

Samir: Where are the artifacts/logs?

Ashwin: Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-traces/hybrid/2026-03-10/1865432100/ (nsys qdrep, summary CSV, nvml logs). Raw perf CSV includes per-request latency and a column trace_mode={none,low,burst}.

profile-bot: [automated] Trace run COMPLETE. Summary CSV available at s3 path above.

Lisa: Can someone add a short runbook for ops: how to disable bursts quickly (toggle in console or api)? If we ever see p99 > SLO, ops must be able to pause tracing in <30s.

Ashwin: Will do — I'll open a PR with the runbook and the alarm -> throttle mapping. Putting draft in #eng-runtime PR in 30m.

Jordan: One more ask: please add a lightweight perf check metric that samples kernel launch count per-second; if launches spike (proxy for many tiny kernels) we should prefer aggregation/merge optimizations before increasing trace level.

Samir: Good call. :thumbsup:
